note: ⚠️ SNG-322 / CCODE-52. The threat ladder: HOW STRONG THIS IS RELATIVE TO YOU, in plain words. Five bands, because the ladder's one job is to make the point where you are outmatched visible and named.
theLine: ⚠️ THE DECISION ERIK LEFT ME: the warned line sits between `hard` and `grave`. At `grave` and above, the encounter is declared lethal, `lethalOfferClamp` fires, and THE PLAYER IS TOLD AND OFFERED A DECLINE. Below it they are not. One line, stated once, and the ladder decides it rather than a flag hand-set per encounter — which was the whole point of CCODE-52.

bands.name: Much weaker than you
bands.meaning: You should win comfortably. Losing would take a run of bad rolls or a bad decision — but it is possible, and being outnumbered or ambushed changes it.

bands.name: An even match
bands.meaning: Either side can win. Expect to be hurt. You can die here on bad luck, the same as anyone can.

bands.name: Stronger than you
bands.meaning: You are likely to lose unless something is in your favour — numbers, ground, preparation. Losing costs you something lasting.
bands.note: ⚠️ WHERE MOST CONTENT SHOULD SIT. Not because it is safe — because it is where a fight is a real question.

bands.name: Much stronger than you
bands.meaning: You are expected to lose. Going down here is likely rather than unlucky, and what happens after you go down is decided by who put you there.
bands.note: ⚠️ THE WARNED LINE, and the warning is about ODDS rather than about death: the player is told they are outmatched and offered a Decline. Everything below can also kill you; this is where it stops being bad luck and starts being the expected outcome.

bands.name: Far beyond you
bands.meaning: There is no version of this fight you win by fighting well. If you engage, you lose; the only questions are how fast and what it costs.
bands.note: ⚠️ SEPARATE FROM `grave` because the game needs a way to say 'this is not a difficulty, it is a wall' — a player meeting a legend at full strength should be told that plainly.

howItIsUsed.decidesLethalFlag: an encounter's `lethal` comes from its band, not from a hand-set field
howItIsUsed.decidesTheOffer: `warn: true` fires lethalOfferClamp — explicit choice plus a Decline option
howItIsUsed.pairsWithAggressorKind: ⚠️ BAND SAYS HOW LIKELY YOU GO DOWN; `aggressorKind` SAYS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU DO. A `grave` beast and a `grave` assassin are equally likely to drop you and completely different afterwards — the beast moves on, the assassin finishes the errand and hides the body. Two dials, two questions, no overlap.

authoringGuidance: Most content should be `fair` or `hard`. If everything is `grave`, nothing is — the warning stops being information and becomes noise, which is the failure mode this ladder exists to prevent.
correction: ⚠️ ERIK CAUGHT THE FIRST NAMES AS FLOWERY AND, WORSE, INACCURATE: 'any of those could kill you.' He is right. 'Beneath notice' and 'An even thing' implied safety, and 'This can kill you' implied the others could not — which is FALSE, because a wild boar can kill you and a bad fall can kill you. The names were doing MOOD WORK instead of INFORMATION WORK. THE BAND MEASURES RELATIVE STRENGTH, NOT LETHALITY. Lethality is what `aggressorKind` and the dice decide. So the names now say only what they measure.
whatTheBandDoesNotSay: ⚠️ IT DOES NOT SAY WHETHER YOU CAN DIE. You can die in any band. The band says HOW LIKELY YOU ARE TO LOSE; `aggressorKind` says WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU DO. A `trivial` assassin will still finish you if the dice go badly — that combination is rare and it is not impossible, and the ladder must never imply otherwise.
